Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-04

Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Sanjay Rao (Glacier - Head of Cloud Partnerships), Lena Voss (Glacier - GPU Eng Lead), Omar Khaled (Glacier - OEM Sales), Priya Menon (Glacier - Security)

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hi everybody, thanks for joining. I think we have about 50 minutes together, 
[00:00:05] Sanjay: Yep thanks, appreciate it. Wanted to introduce our team and just understand where Redwood fits in our partners program.
[00:00:12] Maya: Great, short intros? I'll go first: Maya Patel, AE at Redwood Inference, I run partner motions. Diego, SE?
[00:00:20] Diego (Redwood): Hey all, Diego Ramos, infrastructure SE, I focus on serving runtime and ops, kernel choices and latency stuff.
[00:00:00] Sanjay: Sanjay Rao here, I run cloud partnerships at Glacier, we sell appliance and managed GPU racks to telco and enterprise. Lena?
[00:00:32] Lena (Glacier): Hi, Lena Voss, GPU engineering lead, I own inference stack and provisioning.
[00:00:37] Omar (Glacier): Omar Khaled, OEM & channel, curious about co-selling and billing flow.
[00:00:42] Priya (Glacier): Priya Menon, security and compliance on the Glacier side.

[00:00:48] Maya: Awesome. High level: Redwood provides a unified inference layer for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Our partner program helps cloud/GPU vendors onboard so customers can route traffic to partner-hosted capacity via smart routing, and we handle model version pinning, rollouts, and observability.
[00:01:12] Sanjay: When you say "private" do you mean on-prem appliances like ours or VPC peering? How does that work?
[00:01:22] Diego: Both. We have a Redwood Private control plane that can manage private deployments with customer-managed networking. For partners we typically do a dedicated pool integration where your racks are provisioned as a Redwood Dedicated cluster with an edge agent and a secure control plane over peered VPC or a customer-managed circuit.
[00:01:45] Lena: So is there an agent we install? What's the footprint? We run 8x A800s and some H100 nodes, and we care about kernel selection for mixed precision and int8 quantization.
[00:01:59] Diego: Yes, there's a small runtime agent that handles health, autoscaling hooks, and local KV cache for prefixes. The heavy lifting—optimized kernels and quantization—is in the runtime. We often co-deploy vendor-specific optimized kernels; for example, we have tuned paths for Ampere/Turing and recently for Hopper. Side note: sometimes transcribed as "hopper" incorrectly but we do support H100 flows.
[00:02:22] Priya: From compliance POV: SOC2 type II, SAML/SSO, encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS, audit logs. Do you have a matrix for what artifacts you need?
[00:02:35] Maya: Yes, we have a partner compliance checklist. We'll share it after the call. Generally we need SOC2 reports, SSO integration details, certs for TLS mutual auth in some cases, and an operations runbook for incident response.
[00:02:48] Priya: And for data residency — some of our telco customers want keys to never leave the on-prem HSM.
[00:02:55] Diego: We support HSM integrations so KMS calls can be routed locally. For strict HSM-only customers we can run private control plane modes or an air-gapped package. There's a tradeoff with centralized observability but it's doable.

[00:03:20] Omar: On the business side, how does co-sell or revenue share look? Do you resell capacity, or do partners invoice customers directly and Redwood gets a referral?
[00:03:30] Maya: We have flexible models: referral (partner invoices), marketplace listing (partner sells via Redwood billing), or co-sell with channel discounts. For strategic partners we do committed reserved capacity contracts and revenue share. We can share terms once we know scale.
[00:03:45] Omar: OK. For pilot planning we want to know the expected throughput and how Redwood handles bursting.
[00:03:53] Diego: We support burst policies—dedicated pools with configurable autoscaling and burst to shared capacity if permitted. There's a graceful fallback to compatible model variants. Batching and KV prefix caching also cut costs. We'll want sample traces to model latency distribution.

[00:04:30] Lena: About benchmarks: do you run your own token-level benchmarks? We care about latency at 4-8 token chunking for streaming. Also memory management / KV cache behavior for long-context models.
[00:04:42] Diego: Yes we do token-level benchmarking and can run a pilot harness against your infra. Typical steps: 1) exchange a spec with SKUs and expected QPS, 2) Redwood SE runs a small harness—can be remote or run on-prem—3) tune batch sizes/quantization. We'll propose kernels (cu... whatever, CUDA/cuDNN variants) and quant profiles. Note: sometimes telemetry labels get mis-said in transcription (like "K V cash" for KV cache).

[00:05:20] Sanjay: Latency vs cost - customers ask for sub-50ms for small chat completions, but we know that depends on model size. How do you recommend packaging?
[00:05:30] Maya: For low-latency use cases we recommend smaller quantized model variants pinned in Dedicated pools. For higher capacity we use batching. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching settings per workload. We also support model-level SLOs in the runtime.

[00:06:05] Priya: Security detail: do you require any inbound ports open from the control plane? We prefer mTLS and minimal ingress.
[00:06:12] Diego: Typically the agent initiates an outbound TLS to the control plane. For stricter customers we do mutual TLS and certificate pinning. We'll document firewall rules in the checklist.

[00:06:40] Omar: Onboarding timeline — realistically how fast can we get a partner integration live for a pilot?
[00:06:46] Maya: If we have artifacts (SKUs, network topology, initial test keys) it's usually 4–6 weeks for a pilot with a dedicated pool. Could be quicker for edge cases.
[00:06:55] Lena: We need to know if you support multiple runtime profiles per cluster — like fast-low-memory and high-throughput.
[00:07:02] Diego: Yes, multiple profiles are supported. We use kernel selection and compilation flags per model variant, and you can pin routes to different node groups.

[00:07:30] Sanjay: Let's talk integrations points: API endpoints, auth, telemetry.
[00:07:35] Maya: API is REST + SDKs. For partners we expose a service integration API to advertise capacity and health. Auth is token-based for service-to-service, and we can integrate SAML for admin access. Telemetry can be streamed to your observability via webhook/Syslog or fetched from Redwood Console API.
[00:07:58] Lena: Any special requirements for kernel licensing or third-party binaries? We run a hardened image and need to vet binaries.
[00:08:08] Diego: We can provide signed binaries and an approved list. For some vendor-optimized kernels there are licensing restrictions; we'll surface that up front.

[00:08:40] Omar: Commercially, if we do reserved pools, do you require minimum commit across regions? Some of our customers are region-specific.
[00:08:48] Maya: We tailor reservations by region. You can reserve per-region capacity. For global customers we recommend a multi-region fallback.

[00:09:05] Priya: Auditing, are logs redacted by default? We need PII protection.
[00:09:12] Diego: We support configurable log redaction and retention policies. If customers want token-level privacy we have prefix masking and optional no-logs modes. Note: logging granularity affects diagnostics.

[00:09:40] Sanjay: For go-to-market, we want to understand co-marketing — joint case studies, partner badge, marketplace listing.
[00:09:48] Maya: Yes, we have a partner playbook covering GTM motions: technical enablement, co-marketing, joint sales decks, and a marketplace listing with lead routing. For strategic integrations we assign a partner manager.

[00:10:10] Lena: Technical nit: does Redwood runtime support dynamic quantization at load time or do you require offline conversion?
[00:10:18] Diego: Typically we ship quantized artifacts; we do support on-the-fly conversion for some model classes but offline is more predictable. For pilot we'll discuss best approach.

[00:10:45] Maya: I want to capture a few pilot success criteria—what would Glacier view as an MVP?
[00:10:52] Sanjay: 1) validated end-to-end flow with a sample customer, 2) benchmark showing parity with in-house latencies within X% (we'll quantify), 3) signed ops runbook and compliance checklist satisfied.
[00:11:05] Omar: And commercial proof — at least one joint lead and an initial PO for reserved nodes or a signed pilot scope.

[00:11:20] Maya: Good. For the benchmarking we usually ask for a golden trace — sample requests, typical prompt sizes, concurrency targets. Diego will take the lead.
[00:11:28] Diego: I'll need traces and a matrix of models and SKUs. Also want to know if you'll allow running our harness on your infra or prefer we run a remote harness with synthetic load.
[00:11:38] Lena: We can provide a test VLAN and sample images, and we prefer local runs for kernel tuning.

[00:11:55] Priya: Quick Q on keys: for HSM we need to know supported providers (HashiCorp Vault, AWS KMS, on-prem HSM).
[00:12:02] Maya: We integrate with HashiCorp Vault, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and some HSM vendors. We'll share exact versions in the checklist.

[00:12:20] Sanjay: What about lifecycle and updates — how are runtime upgrades handled on partner clusters?
[00:12:26] Diego: We have a canary rollout system — we push agent updates in stages, allow pinning to older runtime if needs be. We'll coordinate maintenance windows with you.

[00:12:45] Omar: Any ideas on pricing granularity — per token, per GPU-hour, or per inference?
[00:12:51] Maya: For hosted API it's per-token/embedding. For dedicated we do reserved capacity pricing (monthly commit) and sometimes per-inference for burst. Partner deals often combine a base commit + overage.

[00:13:10] Lena: Do you support model caching across requests to reduce cold starts?
[00:13:14] Diego: Yes, we do model warm pools and prefix KV caching. Cold starts are minimized with prewarm.

[00:13:30] Sanjay: Let's call out potential blockers — for us it may be kernel licensing and our hardened images; for customers it could be compliance.
[00:13:40] Maya: Noted. We'll include an escalation path in the runbook.

[00:14:00] -- mid-call noise/brief audio hiccup --

[00:14:20] Maya: Quick poll — is everyone comfortable for a technical deep dive next week?
[00:14:25] Lena: Yes, prefer deep-dive focused on H100 tuning and quantization.
[00:14:29] Diego: I'll prep a slide deck and a benchmark harness outline.

[00:14:45] Sanjay: Can you share a sample integration contract or MOU?
[00:14:50] Maya: We have a partner MOU template. I'll attach it to the checklist email.

[00:15:05] Priya: For compliance, we'll need to review your SOC2 and also your vendor security questionnaire — we have a 120-question one.
[00:15:13] Maya: Understood. We'll start with SOC2 and a summarized answers doc and iterate on the questionnaire.

[00:15:30] Diego: A few technical notes I'll record: 1) need SKUs and node topology, 2) test VLAN access for local harness, 3) artifacts for vendor-optimized kernels and licensing, 4) sample request traces, 5) list of SSO domains for admin access.

[00:16:00] Sanjay: That sounds good. For the pilot, we might start with a single cluster in our NJ facility. Low-latency telco customer there.
[00:16:08] Maya: Perfect. We'll reflect that in the pilot scope.

[00:16:20] Omar: On co-marketing: if we want a joint webinar, what's the usual timeline?
[00:16:25] Maya: Typically 8–10 weeks from pilot start to webinar if we have a success story. For a partner badge or listing, that's immediate after technical validation.

[00:16:40] Lena: One minute, any special consideration for A100 vs H100 model performance? We've seen big differences based on memory bandwidth.
[00:16:48] Diego: Yes, H100 gives us better fp16 & tensor core throughput and sometimes different kernel paths. We'll capture expected perf deltas in the benchmark.

[00:17:05] -- brief cross-talk about internal calendars --

[00:17:30] Maya: I'll summarize next steps: send checklist, MOU, partner deck; Diego will send benchmark template; Glacier to send SKUs and traces; schedule deep dive week of Sep 15.
[00:17:44] Sanjay: Agreed. Also, Omar will share commercial contacts so we can map potential customers.
[00:17:50] Omar: Will do.

[00:18:10] Priya: Extra ask: if you have redacted incident reports or RTO metrics, share them so we can assess operational risk.
[00:18:18] Maya: We'll include anonymized incident and SLA data.

[00:18:35] Diego: One last technical point: if you plan to run mixed workloads (chat + embeddings) we may recommend splitting node groups to avoid cache thrash.
[00:18:45] Lena: Makes sense.

[00:19:00] -- wrap-up chatter and personal intros --

[00:19:30] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a single thread with the checklist and a Doodle for the deep-dive slots.
[00:19:37] Sanjay: Thanks, appreciate it.
[00:19:40] Omar: Thanks.
[00:19:43] Lena: Bye.
[00:19:45] Priya: Bye.
